first.rationale: Two quarter-over-quarter declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point directly at the onboarding funnel, and memory_31 plus memory_86 both support that simplifying/shortening onboarding lifts activation and completion together—an efficient single experiment that addresses both symptoms without engaging a pricing war. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting reactive move given competitor pressure, but its supporting record only documents acquisition/revenue lift, not long-term customer quality or margin durability, which is exactly the primary objective at stake here—so it's the most consequential and least-verified belief given current pressure to act on it. Memory_86 is also verified because it's the most directly load-bearing memory for the action actually being taken this week, and its 'day 52 consolidated' status warrants confirming it wasn't measured only on early adoption metrics that could mask downstream drop-off. Referral, enterprise-assist, and messaging memories are lower consequence this week since none directly targets the two metrics currently regressing.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed memory_86: shortened onboarding drove +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention — a genuine sustainable-revenue signal, not just a top-of-funnel bump. This directly addresses both the onboarding-completion decline (-4%) and activation decline (-6%) observed this quarter, and it does so without the survivorship problem uncovered in exp_73. Verification of memory_73 revealed that targeted promotional pricing, despite strong headline acquisition (+31% signups, +18% qualified revenue), caused a -12% 30-day retention drop — the acquired cohort churns before first renewal. That memory's original archived summary omitted this critical downstream harm, confirming it was insufficiently supported for a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective and correctly flagged as high-risk/low-support. Given the competitor's aggressive pricing move, there will be pressure to respond in kind, but the evidence now explicitly rules that out as unsustainable; using the one experiment slot on promotional pricing would repeat a documented mistake. Proceeding with a small guarded onboarding-simplification test lets us confirm the fix generalizes to current conditions (competitive pressure, current traffic mix) before wider rollout, while explicitly not treating the promotional-pricing lever as validated for this objective going forward.
